unit.title: Small gardens
unit.needIt: You can start a garden even if you think your space is too small. This helps you turn a messy corner into a useful spot for food or beauty.
unit.why: Many people never start a garden because they think they need a huge field. This story shows that a tiny space with a lot of love is better than a big field that is ignored. Small efforts at home are the best way to make a big change.
unit.outcome: Start a small garden in a tiny space.
unit.reachesYou: You see small patches of dirt or weeds in your backyard or near your front door. You might also see small pots of herbs on a kitchen window sill.
unit.do: Find one small corner of your yard or a balcony that has weeds or trash. Clear it out and put one single plant there this week.

quiz.q: Why do some people fail to start a garden?
choices: They think their space is too small
quiz.why: The text says people do not attempt to grow anything because they think they lack a large enough place.
quiz.quote: ANY persons who would like to grow flowers and vegetables do not attempt to grow any because they do not consider that they have a place large enough to justify them in doing so.

quiz.q: What is a key feature of a successful garden?
quiz.why: The text states that attention is one of the important features for success.
quiz.quote: it will be more likely to get more attention than would be given to the larger one, and attention is one of the important features of any successful garden.

quiz.q: What happens to small nooks if they are not used?
quiz.why: The text says these areas will be given over to weeds or rubbish if not improved.
quiz.quote: These, if not improved, will be pretty sure to be given over to weeds, or to the accumulation of rubbish of one kind or another

quiz.why: The text says civic improvement should start at the home.
quiz.quote: this would be done at the very place where civic improvement ought to start, the home.

quiz.q: What is the advice regarding mixing varieties?
quiz.why: The author advises against mixing varieties and prefers one plant per piece of ground.
quiz.quote: I would not advise much mixing of varieties. On the contrary, I would prefer to give over each little piece of ground to one plant.

quiz.q: What is the final rule for small spaces?
choices: One plant is better than none
quiz.why: The text concludes that even one solitary plant is better than having nothing.
quiz.quote: Have flowers and vegetables, even if there isn't room for more than half a dozen plants, or only one plant for that matter, for that one solitary plant will be a great deal better than none at all.

partials: A garden need not be a large one to be enjoyable.
A few plants are better than none.
Small spaces can be more satisfactory because they get more attention.
Not an inch of soil is allowed to go to waste.
One solitary plant will be a great deal better than none at all.
crystal.key: Small spaces and single plants are better than no garden at all.

crystal.aha: Small scale gardening is better than no gardening because attention and small successes lead to growth.
